newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria warns of possible bomb wave before polls.
newsitem.headline: Austria warns of possible bomb wave before polls.

text.p: The Austrian government on Monday warned of possible letterbomb attacks ahead of European parliamentary elections and a Vienna state poll on October 13.
The Interior Ministry urged care when handling unusually heavy letters or packages with oily spots which could have come from plastic explosives.
Austria has been hit by a series of bombings since December 1993 but police, who suspect rightwing extremists, have so far failed to make any arrests in connection with the campaign.
Four gypsies were killed in February 1995 in a booby-trapped bomb blast.
The last wave of letter bombs occurred in December 1995, a week before a snap general election. The bombs exploded prematurely in a postbox and no one was hurt.
The series of letter bombs have often coincided with nationwide or regional polls in the past three years.
Besides the murder of the four gypsies in southeastern Austria, at least 11 others have been injured in five waves of clearly racially-motivated letterbomb attacks and two pipebomb explosions.
More than 20 letter bombs have been posted in the course of the campaign and most have exploded. The majority targeted foreigners and figures linked with immigrant or refugee issues.
